compensation.verdict:
THE POSITIVE DIRECTION OF THIS RULE IS NOT RELIABLE, AND THE NUMBERS SAY SO.
  On the 13 case rows that are INDEPENDENT of the papers the rules were derived from, the rule chain agreed with the published outcome 4 times (31%) -- i.e. it was WRONG MORE OFTEN THAN RIGHT. All 9 of its independent errors are FALSE POSITIVES: it predicted a compensation response where the experimenters looked and found none.
  By contrast it scores 11/12 on the rows drawn from its own source papers. That gap between 11/12 on home ground and 4/13 away from it IS the result: the rule encodes the published mechanism faithfully and still does not predict new cases.
  CAUSE: the rule chain can only see a LESION CLASS, while the outcome turns on the individual ALLELE. El-Brolosy's own data contain two PTC alleles (hbegfa^sa18135, vcla^sa14599) of genes that do adapt, which do not adapt -- and the rule cannot tell them from the alleles that do. A PTC is necessary, not sufficient.
  WHAT THE NEGATIVE DIRECTION IS WORTH: 4 true negatives and 1 false negative. Refusals are far more trustworthy than assertions here, which is the asymmetry the scoring function should exploit.
  ON REAL DATA (mode A) the rule abstains on 24 of 40 rows and decides 1. Our omics layer cannot supply tissue-and-stage expression for a candidate compensator in almost every case, so in production this rule will mostly return 'unknown'. That is the correct behaviour and it should not be "fixed" by relaxing R06.
  RECOMMENDATION TO THE FUNCTIONAL SCORER: do NOT treat 'plausible-by-rule' as compensation. Count only 'documented' AND functional_rescue === true as a met requirement; treat 'plausible-by-rule' as an unmet requirement carrying a flag for human review. Use 'not-expected' with confidence.
compensation.headline: drawn from the papers it was derived from, and 4/13 on cases independent of them (31%). Every one of those 9 independent errors is a false positive: it predicted a compensation response where the experimenters looked and found none.
compensation.scoringRule: a requirement is MET by compensation only on class "documented" AND functional_rescue === true; "plausible-by-rule" is an UNMET requirement with a review flag; "not-expected" is trusted; "unknown" is never a pass

classes.documented: This gene, in this organism, has a published compensation outcome. The verdict is read off the case table, not inferred.
classes.plausible-by-rule: No published outcome for this gene, but every condition of a rule derived from primary evidence is satisfied. Weaker than 'documented' and must never be scored as equal to it.
classes.not-expected: A rule positively excludes compensation (not merely 'no evidence found'). Confident refusal.
classes.unknown: The inputs a rule needs are absent. Explicitly NOT a licence to assume compensation, and explicitly NOT evidence against it.

compensation.renderRule: "plausible-by-rule" is an UNMET requirement with a review flag, never a resolved compensation. A requirement is MET by compensation only on class "documented" AND functional_rescue === true. All nine of the rule's independent errors are false positives: it predicted a compensation response where none was published.

metabolome.why: this repository has no metabolomic dataset. omics/ carries five layers — genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, pathway, ptm — and no metabolite measurement of any organism in this project exists in it.

honesty.finTissue: No PaxDb zebrafish dataset is fin tissue, so no abundance number in this pack is a fin measurement.
honesty.flyingFishProteome: UniProt has no flying-fish proteome (25 entries in Exocoetidae, mostly barcoding fragments); AlphaFold DB has no model for any protein of any gliding mammal in this project's panel. A structural comparison across gliders cannot be done today.

divergenceContext.headline: The winged zebrafish differs from its reference by 2 edited loci and 1 amino acid. In just the 37 causal-chain proteins with medaka orthologues, zebrafish and medaka (same class, different orders) differ by 7300 amino-acid substitutions (16054 positions counting indels) (median identity 79.2%); zebrafish and a bat (Myotis) by 10205 substitutions in 33 proteins (median 74.0%); zebrafish and human by 10765 substitutions in 37 proteins. A handful of edits against thousands of differences in a few dozen proteins, and these are only the coding differences in a tiny gene sample: the genome-wide difference, coding and non-coding, was not measured here and is necessarily larger.

flyingFishOrthologue.why_not_an_orthologue_call: Reciprocal best hit FAILED: the flying-fish protein's best match back in the zebrafish proteome is kcnh7a, not kcnh2a. This is a hit found by searching a zebrafish or medaka protein against the flying-fish set, not an orthologue call, and it must not be reported as one. For a duplicated gene family this is the expected failure mode and it means the paralogue cannot be distinguished at this identity level.

ledger.headline: We can assess 22 of 73 requirements (30.1 %); the other 51 are unassessable, each with a stated reason. Of the 22 assessable differences: 2 have a DEMONSTRATED resolution, 1 rest on a HYPOTHESIS, and 19 are UNRESOLVED. ZERO loci have any flying-fish expression or functional-assay data.

coverage.note: we can assess 22 of 73 requirements; the rest are unassessable, each with its own stated reason. ZERO of the loci have flying-fish expression or functional-assay data of any kind, because no flying-fish transcriptome, proteome, mutant or assay exists in any archive we searched. Every "requirement" is therefore a SEQUENCE STATE in the analogue, never a measured function of the analogue.

resolutionTwoWays.rule: the two fractions are reported separately and are NEVER summed. "Could be compensated" is a hypothesis, not evidence.

ledger.requirementSetScope: The requirement set is the set of loci Daane 2021 reports as KNOWN to differ in flying fishes (74 coding loci against 23,611 predicted genes = 0.31 % of the gene set), plus nothing for the regulatory changes, which cannot be enumerated because the accelerated-CNE sheets give GO terms and no gene names. It is not a causal set and not a complete one.

analogue.operationalDefinition: leaves the water and travels through air over a measurable distance without flapping-powered thrust. Satisfied by a taxon for which a glide distance or duration is reported, or for which the gliding habit is the taxon-defining behaviour in the primary literature.
analogue.basis: satisfies the operational definition of "glides over water after leaving it"
analogue.dataPoorStatement: The ONLY analogue for this function has a genome and nothing else: no transcriptome, no proteome, no expression atlas, no mutant, no functional assay, and 9 of 3,860 genes carry an identifier for it. Every functional requirement derived from it is therefore derived from SEQUENCE and from the curated comparative analysis in one paper - never from a measurement of the analogue doing the thing.

baseGenome.why: a 50:50 WEIGHTED AVERAGE OF SHAPE PARAMETERS is not a genome. The document does not say which allele the chimera carries at any locus, and there is no coherent way to average two genomes, so the design side of every locus-level requirement is unreadable. That is a property of the design, not a gap in the data.

sequence.why: This design has NO genotype. It is a weighted average of two parents' SHAPE parameters. There is no such thing as a 50:50 blended genome, and nothing in the document says which alleles the chimera carries, so no locus-level difference from the analogue can be computed for it at all. That is a property of the design, not a gap in the data.

ledger.scope: A functional-analogue ledger for ONE function, built from the loci one paper reports as known to differ in the analogue. Resolutions above UNRESOLVED carry their evidence and its kind; hypothesised and demonstrated resolutions are reported as two numbers and are never added together. No Aves data (frozen holdout).

chain.weakestLink: molecular_function->process. The step is heavily sourced but the papers disagree on sign: Perathoner 2014 shows the gain-of-function channel hyperpolarizes (oocytes), Jiang 2024 shows Kcnk5b produces net depolarization in fin bud cells via Na+ channels, and Daane 2018 obtains the same growth outcome from a decreased-conductance (I290A) channel. The Ca2+/CaMKK/shha arm is also measured partly in HEK293 cells rather than fin cells. A second weakness: the pectoral-fin-specific link in the last step rests on van Eeden 1996 ('generally longer fins'), read as abstract only.
